To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have proposed a localized routing algorithm for wireless ad hoc networks, based on GFG algorithm and dominating sets that guarantees delivery and is very close to optimal, in terms of hop counts, compared to the shortest-path algorithm.
the shortcut based routing with guaranteed delivery can be performed on dominating set and the excess in the hop count can be reduced to less than half of excess obtained by the basic GFG routing.

we have proposed and analyzed a new localized routing algorithm that combines greedy and FACE routing, with guaranteed delivery, that outperforms existing GFG algorithm, in terms of the average hop count, by a factor of 2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the performance of existing localized routing algorithms for wireless ad hoc networks.

improving performance of existing localized position based routing protocols for wireless networks, by reducing the average hop count, while preserving their desirable properties of low memory requirement and low complexity, and guaranteeing delivery.
the problem of designing localized routing algorithms with guaranteed delivery in wireless networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our proposed routing scheme is the best localized routing algorithm that has been developed so far.

we have proposed a localized algorithm that is close to optimal in terms of hop-count and that has guaranteed delivery, and is applicable for a wide class of networks, including networks with low degree nodes.

the proposed localized algorithm has the following properties: (a) it is guaranteed to deliver messages, (b) it does not require any global knowledge or memorization of past traffic, (c) it has very low excess (compared to shortest path length), and (d) it has a simple structure and can be easily implemented.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the shortcut procedure can be used to improve the performance of any localized position based routing algorithm that uses greedy routing as a main component.
, in the case of connected unit graphs, we have localized algorithms that guarantee delivery of messages, have performance close to the shortest path algorithms and do not depend on past traffic.
we developed a new routing algorithm that guarantees packet delivery in a connected unit graph and has very low hop count.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of localized algorithms can be improved by adding shortcuts and by running the algorithm on the network of internal nodes.
localized routing algorithms can be improved by adding shortcut and sooner-back procedures, and by applying them to a connected dominating set.

, by adding shortcut procedure to GFG algorithm and by running the algorithm on a carefully chosen dominating set, we are able to reduce the average hop count of the routing algorithm to about half of its value with GFG routing.
